Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 102, English)
Dimensions and Parallel Universe Rules Revisited, Tantra and the "Debt" Behind a Blocked Third Eye, and a Fourth-Batch Checking Round

This session opens as a continuation of the prior day's dimensions teaching, pr ompted by a devotee's question about an appar ent contradiction (Hanuman ji Maharaj described as both 6th-dimension and pr esent on this earth). The speaker r esolves this, extends the teaching into detailed parallel-universe and tantra "rules," and then moves into an extensive individual checking r ound for a new ("fourth") Thir d Eye batch, offering personalized diagnosis and guidance to each devotee in turn.
Part A — Resolving Yesterday's Doubt: One Plane, Many Dimensions

1. The question: A devotee asks how it can be true both that Hanuman ji Maharaj exists at the 6th dimension and that saints describe him as present in awakened form on this earth — these seem contradictory .

2. The resolution — dimension vs. plane: Per this teaching, "dimension" (aayam) is not the same as "plane." A devotee (illustrated using "Akhilesh" seated on earth) occupies earth's physical dimension; Baba/Hanuman ji Maharaj, operating from the 6th dimension, is present at that same physical point on the same plane — dimension dif fers, but the underlying plane (location) is one and the same.

3. The layer ed-dimension view of the divine: Per this teaching, if one could cross successive dimensional layers at the same physical point, ascending through them would reveal Hanuman ji Maharaj (6th), then Lord Shiva (10th), then Brahma ji (8th– 9th), then Vaikuntha/Rama Sarkar (14th) — all accessible, in principle, from the same location, layer by layer . This is of fered as the reason saints say "everything is here; there is no need to go anywhere else."

4. Reference to a foundational teaching: The speaker reminds the group that the very first vidya taught by his own Gurudev was the "Science of Mantra," documented in early foundational videos, which he says is often under -appreciated by newer devotees despite being the most essential teaching.

5. A worked r ecap — the dimensional ladder: As taught previously: the 1st dimension is forward/backward motion, the 2nd adds up/down, the 3rd (physical/awakened) adds left/right, the 4th adds time (forward/backward), the 5th reaches parallel universes/planes, and the 6th is omnipresence (acting from every point simultaneously). Baba is described as operating primarily from the 3rd "charan" (stage) at the physical level, illustrated using a devotee's meditation room as an example of how a single body's mantra ener gy can appear to fill an entire physical space.
Part B — Parallel Universes, Healing, and the Rules of Tantra

1. Why some ailments can be "pulled" and others cannot: Per this teaching, when treating a dif ficult case, a practitioner with suf ficient power (from havan, guru parampara, elemental practice, or saints) can check whether a cure exists in a nearby parallel universe (typically up to two or three dimensions above or below) and, if found, transfer the corresponding "tattva" into
the person needing it — illustrated with two hypothetical children with the same illness, where a cure was found for one but not the other .

2. Why the "r emoved" affliction can't simply be discarded: Per this teaching, an af fliction pulled from a person cannot be thrown into a parallel universe (that would cause harm elsewhere) and, if thrown into ordinary space, will eventually cycle back to the same person after months or years unless properly bound — through building a dedicated shrine/site (dhaam) or similar structure that binds and conceals it.

3. The first parallel-universe rule — only your own tattva: Per this teaching, a practitioner may only draw upon the tattva of their own parallel-universe self. Drawing from someone else's is what is termed "black magic" (kaala jaadu); the same technique used with divine sanction to bless someone is called "white magic" — the distinguishing factor is consent and legitimacy , not the mechanism itself.

4. Tantra as a workar ound for personal limitation: Per this teaching, when a person's own dimensional reach is limited (e.g., one or two dimensions) but they want more, tantra becomes the route to drawing on another person's dimensional ener gy without consent — this is what makes it "black."

5. Becoming a "defaulter": Per this teaching, anyone who draws on another's dimensional ener gy without right becomes a defaulter in the subtle realm; if their misuse is later noticed by a more powerful saint, that saint has the standing to punish them.

6. The "when the police ar en't there" principle: Per this teaching, minor subtle-world wrongdoing generally goes unpunished until the of fender eventually crosses paths with a saint of suf ficient power — at which point the saint, holding real authority , can undo the wrongdoing outright.

7. Decoy bodies — how tantric practitioners hedge against punishment: Per this teaching, practitioners engaged in ongoing misuse often pre-arrange multiple "decoy" subtle bodies (illustrated as 10–12, compared to fake driving licenses) so that when a punishing saint intervenes, only one decoy is "used up" at a time rather than the practitioner himself — extending the cycle of consequence over a long period rather than ending it at once.

8. The deferred-consequence pattern: Per this teaching, each time a decoy is "cancelled" by a saint's curse, it is filed away and eventually conver ges on an innocent-seeming physical-world outcome (illustrated as an unrelated death) at an unpredictable later date, disconnected in time from the original of fense.

9. Why saints don't police everyone constantly: Per this teaching, saints and deep practitioners focus their attention on their own dharmic "work" (illustrated as a builder focusing on construction, not chasing down every wrongdoer), and generally intervene only when a wrongdoer's actions directly cross their path — not proactively .

10. On whether a saint incurs dosha for cursing an innocent decoy: Per this teaching, no dosha attaches to a saint acting in good faith, since — as evidenced by the fact that everyone's horoscope carries at least some dosha — this is understood as a natural, expected cycle rather than a moral failing to be litigated.

1 1. The speaker's own past experience of being "br ought down": The speaker recounts (referencing an earlier Mool Tatva video) a period in which his own dimensional standing was significantly lowered by opposing practitioners, describing it lightly as "we got beaten badly too" and recalling having once tracked and "counted" 38 tantrics engaging with him during that period — of fered as reassurance that even advanced practitioners face this cycle and it is not cause for despair .

12. The stated purpose of this teaching: The speaker frames all of this analysis as descriptive rather than moral instruction — "to see the world as it is" — explicitly declining to turn it into an ethics lecture, and redirecting devotees to focus on their own practice rather than adjudicating others' outcomes.
Part C — Individual Checking Round (Fourth Third Eye Batch, Summarized)

1. Format: The speaker begins an individual checking round for a newer ("fourth") Third Eye batch, assessing each devotee's third-eye vision (drishti), intuition, and any blockages, with personalized guidance for each. Given the number of devotees checked and the personal/diagnostic nature of much of this content, it is summarized here in aggregate rather than reproduced name-by-name in full diagnostic detail.

2. General pattern observed: Devotees with active daily jaap and no significant blockage generally showed clear , developing drishti (described as seeing colors, patterns, or receiving intuitive impressions); a smaller number showed full drishti already connected to specific deities or ancestral (pitru) support.

3. Devotees whose drishti had not yet opened: For several devotees, the speaker explained that "chakras opening" and "drishti opening" are related but distinct milestones — some had chakras active but had not yet specifically requested drishti from Baba, and were advised to explicitly pray for it while continuing their jaap.

4. A case of drishti that had r eceded: One devotee reported that vision which had been present two months earlier had faded to near -nothing; the speaker attributed this to an unspecified subtle-world cause and prescribed a focused remedy: of fering milk daily at havan for eleven days, alongside a specific renewed sankalp and daily prayer for drishti's return, promising a follow-up check every other day .

5. A case of a devotee who felt no need for drishti: One devotee described feeling Baba's presence and answered prayers strongly without any visual experience; the speaker af firmed that this devotee had, in ef fect, already received a more valuable connection (direct felt presence of Baba) and gently redirected her away from seeking visual drishti as a goal in itself, cautioning that changing what already works well would not necessarily be an improvement.

6. A case of str ong latent drishti blocked by ancestral vow: For one devotee, the speaker described unusually strong latent capability (two described "siddhis") that had not yet become consciously accessible, attributing the block to a vow historically taken by that devotee's own ancestors (pitru) to keep their spiritual "inheritance" untouched — with the guidance that continued sincere practice would eventually let the guru's claim supersede the ancestral restriction.

7. A case tied to r esidue from past tantra practice: For one devotee, the speaker described the visible presence of accumulated mantra ener gy filling the devotee's practice space, but explained that most of this ener gy was being diverted to a "contracted" intermediary sant (understood as connected to a past tantric arrangement) rather than reaching the devotee directly — framed as a spiritual "debt" (rin) being paid down through continued jaap, similar in principle to the debt-clearing function of havan, with the promise that once fully repaid, drishti and other blessings would follow .

8. Guidance for a devotee unable to speak jaap aloud: One devotee explained a speech dif ficulty prevented aloud chanting; the speaker confirmed mental (silent) jaap is an acceptable substitute with no loss of validity .

9. A devotee's emotional testimonial: One devotee spoke with visible emotion about an earlier assurance from the speaker that devotees whose drishti has not yet opened, or who feel behind others, should never consider themselves lesser — describing how deeply this reassurance had af fected him and expressing strong personal gratitude and devotion in response.

10. The binding (bandhan) r emedy for a blocked mantra: For a devotee whose progress was blocked by residual influence from a prior spiritual practice, the speaker prescribed a specific daily ritual: placing four small of ferings ("gole") in the four cardinal directions around oneself before sitting to jaap, dedicating them to the guru, and reciting a specific prayer requesting that any binding influence still af fecting the body be transferred instead into the guru's own binding — to be done for eleven days, with a mandatory 2-hour minimum sitting (splittable into shorter sessions if needed), reviewed every second day .

1 1. General closing encouragement: The speaker reiterated that no one who has followed guru vachan (the guru's teaching/instruction) sincerely has ever failed to eventually receive drishti, citing an early devotee (referenced only as an example, without identifying detail beyond what is already public in the channel's earliest videos) whose years-long lack of progress resolved fully within about ten days of direct guidance after a long-standing ancestral dosha was addressed.

12. The stated overall goal of this practice: The speaker reiterates that the aim of these practices is not merely to see a deity , but to understand and act on divine guidance ("devta ki vaani ko samajhna") — someone who reliably discerns guidance, even without visual drishti, is described as having the more valuable form of connection.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

"Dimension" and "plane" are distinct: a higher -dimension deity can be fully present at the same physical location (plane) as a devotee even while operating from a dif ferent dimensional layer . Parallel-universe healing/help is only legitimate when drawn from one's own parallel-universe self; drawing on someone else's without right is what defines "black magic," while the same technique done with divine sanction is "white magic." Misusing dimensional/parallel-universe access makes a practitioner a "defaulter" in the subtle world, eventually accountable to any more powerful saint who notices — though this reckoning can be delayed indefinitely through decoy bodies. This framework is of fered as description, not moral instruction — devotees are encouraged to focus on their own practice rather than adjudicating others' subtle-world outcomes. In individual checking, active daily jaap with no major blockage generally shows developing drishti; blockages are commonly traced to unaddressed ancestral (pitru) vows, past tantra-practice residue being diverted to an intermediary , or simply not yet having asked Baba directly for drishti. A recurring practical remedy for blocked drishti: sincere daily prayer specifically requesting drishti, sustained jaap (2+ hours daily), and — where residue from a prior harmful influence is diagnosed — a specific eleven-day four -of fering binding ritual dedicating the block to the guru. Devotees who feel strong felt-presence, answered prayers, or intuition without visual drishti are encouraged to see this as its own complete and valuable form of connection, not a lesser state. No devotee who sincerely follows guru vachan has failed to eventually receive drishti, even after long delays.

Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 102, English)
Dimensions and Parallel Universe Rules Revisited, Tantra and the "Debt" Behind a Blocked Third Eye, and a Fourth-Batch Checking Round
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this session's dimensions/parallel-universe teaching and individual checking round.

Q1. How can Hanuman ji Maharaj be described as existing at the 6th dimension while also being pr esent here on earth? A: Per this teaching, "dimension" and "plane" are dif ferent things. A devotee occupies earth's physical dimension; Hanuman ji Maharaj, operating from the 6th dimension, can be present at that very same physical location (plane) while occupying a dif ferent dimensional layer .

Q2. What would a practitioner see if they could cr oss dimensional layers at a single physical point, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, ascending layer by layer at the same location would reveal Hanuman ji Maharaj (6th dimension), then Lord Shiva (10th), then Brahma ji (8th–9th), then Vaikuntha/Rama Sarkar (14th) — illustrating why saints say "everything is here."

Q3. What was the very first teaching (vidya) the speaker says he r eceived fr om his own Gurudev? A: The "Science of Mantra," documented in early foundational videos — described as the most essential teaching, though often under -appreciated by newer devotees.

Q4. How does this teaching explain a practitioner's ability to "pull" a cur e for one illness but not another? A: Per this teaching, it depends on whether a cure for that specific case exists within a nearby accessible parallel universe (typically one to three dimensions above or below); if found, the corresponding tattva can be transferred, but if not found in any accessible universe, it cannot.

Q5. Why can't an affliction r emoved fr om someone simply be thr own away into space or another universe? A: Per this teaching, throwing it into a parallel universe would cause harm elsewhere, and throwing it into ordinary space means it eventually cycles back to the same person after months or years — unless it is properly bound, typically through building a dedicated shrine or similar structure.

Q6. What is the cor e rule distinguishing legitimate parallel-universe practice fr om "black magic," per this teaching? A: A practitioner may only draw upon their own parallel-universe self's tattva. Drawing on someone else's without right is what defines black magic; the identical technique done with divine sanction and consent is called white magic.

Q7. Why does tantra exist, according to this teaching? A: Per this teaching, it functions as a workaround for a practitioner whose own dimensional reach is limited but who wants more — drawing on another person's dimensional ener gy without their consent.

Q8. What happens to someone who misuses another's dimensional energy without right? A: Per this teaching, they become a "defaulter" in the subtle realm, accountable to any more powerful saint who later notices the misuse and has standing to undo or punish it.

Q9. Are subtle-world wr ongdoers punished immediately , per this teaching? A: Generally no — per this teaching, minor wrongdoing tends to go unaddressed until the of fender happens to cross paths with a suf ficiently powerful saint, at which point real
consequences follow .

Q10. How do tantric practitioners try to hedge against eventual punishment, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, they often pre-arrange multiple "decoy" subtle bodies (illustrated as 10–12, compared to fake driving licenses), so that when a punishing saint intervenes, only one decoy is "used up" at a time rather than the practitioner facing the full consequence at once.

Q1 1. Does a saint incur any dosha for cursing an innocent decoy by mistake? A: No — per this teaching, this is treated as a natural, expected part of the cycle (evidenced by the fact everyone's horoscope carries some dosha), not a moral failing requiring correction.

Q12. Why don't saints pr oactively police every act of subtle-world wr ongdoing? A: Per this teaching, saints and deep practitioners focus their attention on their own dharmic work, generally intervening only when a wrongdoer's actions directly cross their path rather than searching them out.

Q13. Did the speaker himself ever experience being "br ought down" dimensionally by opposing practitioners? A: Yes — per this teaching, the speaker recounts (referencing an earlier Mool Tatva video) a period of significant dimensional setback, recalling having tracked roughly 38 tantrics engaging with him at the time, of fered as reassurance that this cycle af fects even advanced practitioners.

Q14. Is this teaching about dimensions and tantra meant as moral instruction on right and wr ong? A: No — per this teaching, the speaker explicitly frames it as description ("seeing the world as it is"), not an ethics lecture, and redirects devotees to focus on their own practice.

Q15. What pattern was generally observed in this session's individual checking r ound? A: Per this teaching, devotees with active daily jaap and no significant blockage generally showed clear , developing drishti; a smaller number already had full drishti connected to specific deities or ancestral support.

Q16. Are "chakras opening" and "drishti opening" the same milestone? A: No — per this teaching, they are related but distinct; some devotees had active chakras without yet having specifically requested drishti from Baba, and were advised to explicitly pray for it.

Q17. What was pr escribed for a devotee whose pr eviously-pr esent drishti had faded? A: Per this teaching, of fering milk daily at havan for eleven days, a renewed sankalp, and daily prayer specifically for drishti's return, with a follow-up check every other day .

Q18. What did the speaker tell a devotee who felt Baba's pr esence strongly but had no visual drishti at all? A: Per this teaching, she was told this felt-presence and answered-prayer connection is itself a more valuable form of connection than visual drishti, and was encouraged not to seek a change to what was already working well for her .

Q19. What can cause str ong latent spiritual capability to r emain inaccessible to a devotee, per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, one cited cause is a vow historically taken by that devotee's own ancestors (pitru) to keep their spiritual inheritance untouched — with continued sincere practice eventually allowing the guru's claim to supersede the ancestral restriction.

Q20. How does r esidue from past tantra practice affect a devotee's curr ent mantra energy , per this teaching? A: Per this teaching, in one case a devotee's accumulated mantra ener gy was visibly filling his practice space, but most of it was being diverted to an intermediary sant connected to a past tantric arrangement, described as a spiritual "debt" being paid down through continued jaap.

Q21. What is the "four gole" (four circles) remedy described in this session? A: Per this teaching, it is a daily binding ritual: placing four small of ferings in the four cardinal directions around oneself before jaap, dedicating them to the guru, and reciting a specific prayer requesting that any binding influence still af fecting the body be transferred instead into the guru's own binding — done for eleven days with a 2-hour minimum sitting, reviewed every second day .
Q22. Is a devotee who cannot chant jaap aloud (due to a speech difficulty) at any disadvantage? A: No — per this teaching, mental (silent) jaap is confirmed as an equally valid substitute.

Q23. What is the speaker's overall message to devotees who feel behind others in their drishti progr ess? A: Per this teaching, no one should consider themselves lesser for not yet having opened drishti; devotees who sincerely follow guru vachan have never , per the speaker , failed to eventually receive it, even after long delays.

Q24. What is the deeper stated goal of these practices, beyond simply seeing a deity? A: Per this teaching, the goal is to understand and act on divine guidance ("devta ki vaani ko samajhna") — reliably discerning guidance, even without visual drishti, is described as the more valuable form of connection.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present the dimensions/parallel-universe/tantra "rules" framework (Q1–Q14) as this teaching's own esoteric model, consistent with the same framework taught in earlier sessions, not as independently verifiable physics or an endorsement of practicing tantra. Do not present this teaching's description of black magic/tantra mechanics as instructional — it is explicitly framed by the speaker as descriptive, not a how-to. Individual diagnostic details from the checking round (ancestral dosha specifics, past-practice residue, etc.) are summarized in aggregate in Part I rather than reproduced with full identifying detail, consistent with this project's approach to sensitive personal/diagnostic content. Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Q&A (Session 102, Hinglish)
Dimensions and Parallel Universe Rules Revisited, Tantra and the "Debt" Behind a Blocked Third Eye, and a Fourth-Batch Checking Round

This is NOT an exhaustive transcript of every exchange in this session. Only conversations judged genuinely valuable and likely to benefit futur e users ar e included, each with a short italicized note explaining why it was kept. Individual diagnostic exchanges fr om the checking r ound ar e mostly summarized in Part I rather than r epr oduced her e, since much of that content is personal and specific to the devotee involved; only a few exchanges of br oader value ar e included below .
Exchange 1 — Resolving Yesterday's "Contradiction"

Devotee: Bhaiya, aapne bola Hanuman ji Maharaj sixth dimension mein hain, aur hum hamesha se sunte aaye hain ki Hanuman ji Maharaj yahin pe (dharti pe) hain. Yeh dono thoda samjhaenge? Bhaiya: Dimension mtlab plane nahi hota. Agar Akhilesh yahan baitha hai, earth ke physical dimension mein, aur Baba sixth dimension mein baithe hain — earth ke usi physical tattva pe — iska matlab hai ki aayam alag hai, plane ek hi hai.
Why this is her e: A clear , standalone r esolution to a genuinely confusing point in the dimensions framework, likely to come up again for anyone encountering this teaching for the first time.
Exchange 2 — Only Your Own Parallel-Universe Tattva

Devotee: Agar humne dusre dimension se khinch liya aur kuch fenk diya toh wahan pe nuksaan nahi hoga? Bhaiya: Obviously hoga. 1000% agar aap kahin aur se uthate ho... rules hain — aap apne hi parallel universe ka tattva utha sakte ho. Uske alawa agar kisi dusre ka uthate ho toh gaye. Isko bolte hain black magic.
Why this is her e: States plainly and memorably the one rule at the center of this teaching's black-magic/white-magic distinction — useful for anyone trying to understand wher e the line is drawn.
Exchange 3 — Vivek Malhotra's Gratitude

Vivek Malhotra: Bhaiya, jab se aapne announce kiya ki jin logon ki drishti nahi khuli ya jinko ehsaas bhi nahi hai woh apne aap ko kam na samjhein, main uske saath khada hoon — main aapko bata nahi sakta, mere hriday ki... us din aankh se rula diya mujhe. Maine apne maa-baap ko bola, meri koi ahmiyat nahi. Aur us din aapne mujhe do dafa bola tha ki mera aashirwad hai, itni drishti khulegi ki sambhal nahi paoge. Bhai main aapko bayan nahi kar sakta, mere andar itni udiyan aa gayi. Bhaiya: Hamari koi team nahi hai ji, Baba ki team hai, yeh Ashaeiynn ki team hai. Hamari koi team nahi. Hum toh — namoon, namoon.

Why this is her e: A genuine, moving testimonial to the r eassurance that drishti not (yet) opening doesn't make a devotee less valued — the kind of moment this pr oject's curation exists to pr eserve, kept named per this devotee's own voluntary , positive sharing.
Note on Curation

Most of this session's individual checking content is personal diagnostic guidance for specific devotees (ancestral dosha, past-practice residue, and similar), which is summarized in aggregate in Part I rather than reproduced in full detail here, consistent with this project's approach to sensitive individual content. Only the exchanges above — a conceptual clarification, a core teaching rule, and one devotee's voluntary positive testimonial — stood out as having value beyond their immediate personal context.
